after.worked_solution:
We wish to add the following fractions:

$$
p+q=\frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{9-4y}{1-2y}
$$

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $5(1-2y)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{9-4y}{1-2y} & = \\ \frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{5}{5}\cdot \frac{9-4y}{1-2y} & = \\ \frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{5(9-4y)}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{6y+5(9-4y)}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{6y+45-20y}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{-14y+45}{5(1-2y)} & \end{aligned}
$$
